key_developments: Canada September CPI on 19 Oct printed 3.1% against 3.2% expected, with trim at 1.8% and median at 1.9%, yet BoC October hike odds held near 70–80% and USD/CAD closed through its 1.4140 stop at 1.41113.

OAT-Bund widened every session from 142.3bp on 19 Oct to a cycle-high 174.6bp on 22 Oct and ended the week at 171.8bp; Moody's affirmed France at Aa3 negative after the 23 Oct close, against expectations of a downgrade.
RBA Deputy Governor Hauser said on 21 Oct the inflation outlook was 'materially worse', lifting November hike odds from 22% to about 51%; Goldman moved to a November hike.
UK unemployment fell to 4.7% on 20 Oct and September CPI printed 3.5% against 3.4% on 21 Oct, taking BoE November hike odds to about 85%; GBP/USD closed through its 1.3365 stop at 1.33798.
NZ Q3 CPI on 21 Oct rose 3.7% y/y against 3.8% expected, but RBNZ October hike pricing stayed near 98%.
A 22 Oct risk-off session (AI earnings, Brent above $110 after Houthi attacks) took USD/JPY down 134 pips and AUD/JPY down 113 pips without any BoJ repricing.
new_risks_identified: French stress is now driven by social unrest as well as fiscal slippage: the 17 Oct riots preceded the OAT-Bund move to 174.6bp.
Moody's affirmation of France after the 23 Oct close is not in prices and is a positive euro shock landing on the EUR/USD and EUR/SGD shorts at Monday's open.
The BoC is treating Brent above $110 as a reason to hike, reversing the oil-precondition channel the CAD-short cluster relied on.
The yen and franc bid together on safe-haven demand on 22 Oct, independent of BoJ or SNB policy, a channel that hits AUD/JPY and the franc-funded longs.
consensus_shifts: BoC October hike odds rose to about 70–80% from the 20–22% assigned at analysis.
RBA November hike odds rose from 22% to about 51% after Hauser on 21 Oct; Goldman joined ANZ and UBS in forecasting a November hike.
Nomura, Rabobank and ING previewed an ECB hold on 29 Oct, with Nomura calling market pricing excessive.
83% of surveyed BoJ watchers now expect a December hike, up from 35%, and none expect 30 Oct.
RBNZ October hike pricing rose from about 58% to about 98%, with 50bp priced by end-February.
Markets price about 84% for a Fed hold on 28 Oct and about 90% for a December hike.
